people.title: Accounts
people.intro: Every mailbox on this server: people and services.

create.title: Add account
create.name: Name
create.ownPasswordHint: Instead of an invitation link. The person can change it later.
create.noDomains: There is no domain yet. Add one first.
create.kindPersonHint: Signs in to the portal and has a mailbox.
create.kindServiceHint: For programs: no portal login, app passwords only. Calendars and contacts start out off.
create.makePassword: Create an app password right away
create.makePasswordHint: Shown exactly once. You can add another one whenever you like.

invite.title: {{name}} has been added
invite.body: Send this link to {{name}} to choose their own password. It works only once.

detail.name: Name
detail.accessHint: For new people or forgotten passwords. The link works once and for 7 days.
detail.createLink: Create a link to choose a password
detail.setPasswordHint: This logs the person out everywhere.
detail.disableHint: Can no longer log in. Mail keeps arriving.
detail.trashHint: Locked at once and no new mail. Can be restored for 30 days.

banner.invited: Has not chosen a password yet.
banner.disabled: Locked: cannot log in, mail keeps arriving.
banner.deleted: In the trash. Will be deleted for good on {{date}}.

detail.aliasLimitHint: How many addresses this person may create on open domains.
detail.sendAsHint: This person may send with any address of these domains, even addresses that do not exist. Handy for a shared office.
detail.convertToServiceHint: For a mailbox that belongs to a program.
detail.convertToServiceBody: There is no portal login afterwards. Two-factor sign-in, passkeys and open sessions are removed; the password so far lives on as an app password that never expires. The mail stays where it is.
detail.convertToPersonHint: For a mailbox that belongs to someone after all.
detail.convertToPersonBody: The account may sign in to the portal again as soon as you set a password or send an invitation link. Its app passwords stay.

purge.title: Delete {{login}} for good?
purge.body: All mail and settings will be gone forever. Type the address to confirm.

security.title: Login
security.appsOnly: mail apps only with app passwords
security.resetHint: Lost the phone and the recovery codes? After a reset, the password is enough again.
security.resetBody: The authenticator app, passkeys and recovery codes are removed. The person gets a notice. Only do this when you know for sure they asked you to.

created.title: {{name}} is ready
created.body: The app password is only here now. After this you can only create a new one.

protocols.title: Protocols
protocols.hint: What this account may use. A protocol that is off lets nobody through, whatever password is typed.
protocols.smtpHint: May send mail through this server.
protocols.imapHint: Mail apps like Thunderbird or Apple Mail.
protocols.jmapHint: UwUMail and anything else that speaks JMAP.
protocols.noMailbox: Without IMAP and JMAP this account has no mailbox.
protocols.redirectHint: An address on this server. Empty: mail to this account is refused at the door.
protocols.redirectNone: Mail to this account is refused.
protocols.redirectTo: Mail to this account goes to {{address}}.
protocols.webmailHint: Opening this mailbox at /mail with the portal login. Separate from IMAP and JMAP, which decide what mail programs may do.

serviceAccess.title: Access
serviceAccess.hint: A service never signs in to the portal. The way in is an app password, and you create those here.
serviceAccess.none: No app password yet. Without one the service gets in nowhere.
serviceAccess.name: What is the password for?
serviceAccess.revokeBody: Whatever uses this password stops getting in.

domains.title: Domains
domains.intro: The domains this server accepts mail for.

empty.title: No domain yet
empty.body: Add the domain this server should receive mail for.

create.title: Add domain
create.name: Domain
create.hint: The domain must be yours. The DNS records it needs come in the next step.

detail.dnsIntro: Your DNS provider needs these records. After a change, just check again.
detail.neverChecked: Not checked yet. The check takes a few seconds.
detail.sourceResolver: Outgoing DNS is blocked here, so the server's resolver answered. New records may show up a little later.
detail.upstream: Mail for this domain arrives through an upstream mail server, so the MX record may point to it.
detail.relay: Outgoing mail leaves through {{relay}}. SPF must allow that server.
detail.name: Name
detail.differs: The record works, it is just written differently than UwUMail would publish it.
detail.nameHint: Some DNS providers want only the part before {{domain}} as the name.

purpose.mx: Tells other mail servers where mail for this domain goes.
purpose.spf: Says which servers may send on behalf of the domain.
purpose.dmarc: Tells recipients what to do with forged mail.
purpose.dkim: Public key recipients use to check the signature of your mail.
purpose.tlsrpt: Other mail servers send reports here about whether encrypted connections to your server work.
purpose.mtasts: Announces the MTA-STS policy. The id changes whenever the policy does.
purpose.mtastsHost: Other servers fetch the policy from this name. It has to point to this server.
purpose.mtastsPolicy: This is the policy as other servers see it. UwUMail serves it itself.
purpose.jmap: Lets apps like UwUMail find the server when you only enter your mail address.
purpose.imaps: Tells mail apps where to read mail (IMAP, port 993).
purpose.submissions: Tells mail apps where to send mail with TLS (port 465).
purpose.submission: Tells mail apps where to send mail with STARTTLS (port 587).

notes.mxUpstream: Points to the upstream mail server. That's fine.
notes.mxElsewhere: Points to another server, so mail will not arrive here.
notes.spfTooLoose: Allows any server to send. Better end it with -all.
notes.spfMultiple: There are several SPF records. Only one is allowed.
notes.spfNotAllowed: Does not allow the sending server. Mail then often lands in spam.
notes.spfUnverified: The address of the sending server could not be found.
notes.dmarcNone: Policy “none”: good for testing. Later switch to quarantine or reject.
notes.dmarcInvalid: The policy (p=) is missing or invalid.
notes.dmarcMultiple: There are several DMARC records. Only one is allowed.
notes.lookupFailed: The lookup failed. Try again in a moment.
notes.dmarcReportsElsewhere: Reports go to another address. With rua=mailto:dmarc-reports@… UwUMail reads them itself.
notes.srvElsewhere: Points to another server or port.
notes.tlsRptElsewhere: Reports go to another address, so UwUMail does not see them.
notes.tlsRptMultiple: There are several TLS reporting records. Only one is allowed.
notes.mtaStsOldId: Has an old id. Other servers only fetch the new policy once the id matches.
notes.mtaStsMultiple: There are several MTA-STS records. Only one is allowed.
notes.mtaStsFetchFailed: The policy could not be fetched. Check the mta-sts name and the certificate.
notes.mtaStsPolicyDiffers: A different policy is served there. Maybe another server answers for that name.
notes.mtaStsPolicyInvalid: No valid policy is served there.

detail.catchAllHint: Mail to addresses that don't exist goes to this person. It also attracts more spam.
detail.keysIntro: The server signs every outgoing mail with these. Switching to new keys now and then is good practice.
detail.rotateSteps: Add the new records above at your DNS provider, check them, then switch over. The old keys keep working until then.
detail.retiredHint: Keep retired keys in DNS for a few days until all mail has been delivered, then remove them.
detail.removeHint: Only possible when no address uses the domain anymore.
detail.selfServiceHint: People may create extra addresses on this domain themselves, up to their limit.
detail.recommendedIntro: Mail works without these records. With them, apps find the server on their own and you get reports when something goes wrong.

forwards.title: Forwarding addresses
forwards.explain: Addresses without a mailbox of their own: mail to them goes straight on, to people here or to other servers. Mail recognized as spam is not passed on.
forwards.edit: Put into the form to change it
forwards.removeConfirm: Really remove {{address}}? Mail to the address is refused then.
forwards.targetsHint: One or more addresses, one per line or separated by commas. If the address exists, its targets are replaced.

mtaSts.title: MTA-STS
mtaSts.intro: With MTA-STS your domain tells other mail servers: mail for me only encrypted, and only to my real server. That way nobody can read along or divert mail on the way.

explain.off: Other servers encrypt when they can, but they do not have to.
explain.testing: Other servers report problems through TLS reports but still deliver. Good for having a look first.
explain.enforce: Other servers only deliver encrypted, to a server with a valid certificate. If that fails, the mail waits on their side.

mtaSts.records: Add the new records from the DNS list above: _mta-sts, mta-sts and _smtp._tls.
mtaSts.enforceConfirm: In enforce mode, other servers only deliver when encryption and certificate are right. Switch now?
mtaSts.ready: Other servers have reported no TLS problems for 14 days. You can switch MTA-STS to enforce.

reports.title: Reports
reports.empty: No reports arrived in the last {{days}} days.
reports.emptyHint: Big providers like Google or Microsoft send reports to dmarc-reports@{{domain}} and tls-reports@{{domain}} once a day, as soon as the DNS records are right.
reports.dmarcIntro: Receivers report how many messages with your domain as the sender reached them and whether SPF or DKIM matched.
reports.noneOfKind: No reports of this kind yet.
reports.ownFailing_one: Messages from one address of this server failed DMARC. Check SPF and DKIM.
reports.ownFailing_other: Messages from {{count}} addresses of this server failed DMARC. Check SPF and DKIM.
reports.stricter: For 14 days, all mail from this server has passed DMARC. You can change the policy from {{from}} to {{to}}:
reports.strangers: Unknown addresses that fail are usually spam in your name. That is exactly what DMARC protects against.
reports.tlsIntro: Other mail servers report whether encrypted connections to your server worked.

results.certificate-host-mismatch: Certificate does not match the name

reports.unauthenticated_one: One report came from a sender that could not prove who it is. Its numbers could be made up.
reports.unauthenticated_other: {{count}} reports came from senders that could not prove who they are. Their numbers could be made up.

reports.title: Reports
reports.intro: What other mail servers report back about your domains.
reports.explain: Big providers send a summary every day: DMARC says how much mail went out in your name and how much of it was taken as genuine, TLS reports say whether the connections to your server were encrypted. The server reads them by itself; the numbers are here.
reports.none: No report arrived in the last {{days}} days. That is normal while there is little mail in your name -- the big providers only speak up once they see some.
reports.someFailed_one: {{count}} message did not pass as genuine, across {{sources}} sending addresses.
reports.someFailed_other: {{count}} messages did not pass as genuine, across {{sources}} sending addresses.
reports.ownFailing_one: An address this server sends from itself fails DMARC. That is worth a look: the domain's page says what fails.
reports.ownFailing_other: {{count}} addresses this server sends from itself fail DMARC. That is worth a look: the domain's page says what fails.
reports.addressTaken: A mailbox or alias sits on {{addresses}}. While it does, the reports land there and are not read.
reports.noneOfKind: Nothing of this kind has arrived yet.
reports.unauthenticated: This report came from a sender who could not prove who they are. Its numbers may be made up.
reports.noRows: The report names no single sending address.
reports.noFailures: No failed session -- everything was encrypted.

noDomains.title: No domain yet
noDomains.body: Reports arrive once a domain is set up and mail has gone out in its name.

host.title: This machine
host.noReport: The helper on this machine has not said anything for a while. Is uwumail-host-machine.timer still running?
host.notApt: This machine does not use apt. UwUMail cannot say what it needs -- that one stays yours.
host.upToDate: Nothing to do: the system is up to date.
host.waiting_one: {{count}} package is waiting, {{security}} of them security updates.
host.waiting_other: {{count}} packages are waiting, {{security}} of them security updates.
host.rebootNeeded: A restart is due for the updates to take hold.
host.notAlone: More runs on this machine: {{others}}. An update restarts those too, and a restart takes them with it.
host.cannotTell: I cannot tell what else runs here. Better look for yourself before pressing the button.
host.liability: What happens here happens on your machine. I look first, as well as I can -- I cannot answer for it.

queue.title: Queue
queue.intro: Outgoing mail that has not reached all recipients yet. Subjects and content are not shown here.

empty.title: Nothing is waiting
empty.body: All mail is on its way or delivered.

queue.dropConfirm: Delete message #{{id}} without notifying the sender?

toasts.retry: Will be retried in a moment

logs.title: Logs
logs.intro: The newest lines of the server log, live.
logs.unavailable: This server keeps no logs for the admin panel.

loki.title: Send to Grafana Loki
loki.intro: Sends the logs of this server and its gateway to a Grafana Loki, such as your own log server or Grafana Cloud.
loki.enabledHint: New lines go out in batches every few seconds. While Loki can't be reached, the server waits and keeps trying, and mail never has to wait for it.
loki.privacyText: Log lines contain personal data: login names and email addresses, IP addresses of mail apps and other servers, senders of received mail. Switching this on sends that data off this server, and it stays in Loki for as long as Loki keeps it. Make sure that is fine for every mailbox on this server.
loki.privacyConsent: I understand and allow the logs, with this data in them, to be sent to the address below.
loki.urlHint: e.g. http://192.168.1.20:3100 or https://logs-prod-012.grafana.net. /loki/api/v1/push is added when the address has no path.
loki.secretSet: Stored. Type a new value to replace it.
loki.tenantHint: Only for a Loki with more than one tenant.
loki.labelsHint: One per line as name=value. The server sets app, instance, source and level itself.
loki.gatewayHint: The UwUMail Gateway's lines come here through the tunnel and go on with the label source=gateway.
loki.testOk: The test line arrived in Loki.

status.error: Loki isn't taking anything right now: {{error}}

settings.title: Settings
settings.intro: For the whole server. Changes take effect at once, without a restart.
settings.fileNote: Whatever {{file}} or UWUMAIL_* environment variables set takes precedence and is locked here.
settings.envNote: Whatever UWUMAIL_* environment variables set takes precedence and is locked here.
settings.spamHint: The spam filter, with allowed and blocked senders, has a page of its own.

tone.title: Mail from the server
tone.intro: Notices about undeliverable mail and automatic replies.
tone.internalHint: Mail to people on this server.
tone.externalHint: Mail to everyone else, e.g. when a message cannot be delivered.

delivery.title: Sending
delivery.intro: How mail leaves for other servers.
delivery.directHint: The server delivers to the recipients' mail servers itself. Port 25 must be open and the IP must have a good reputation.
delivery.directViaGatewayHint: The server delivers to the recipients' mail servers itself, but it leaves through the gateway. Port 25 and the address's reputation count there, not here.
delivery.relayHint: Everything goes through another mail server, e.g. when your connection blocks port 25.
delivery.gatewayNote: Outgoing mail leaves this server through your UwUMail Gateway, with any route set here, "Direct" included. Nothing needs changing here for that.
delivery.passwordSet: Saved. Leave empty to keep it.
delivery.requireTlsHint: Servers without encryption get no mail. Safer, but some recipients become unreachable.
delivery.lifetimeHint: How long the server keeps retrying before the sender gets a notice.
delivery.allowForwardingHint: People may forward their mail to addresses elsewhere once the address agrees. Forwarded mail gets a rewritten sender (SRS).

receiving.title: Receiving
receiving.intro: Limits for incoming mail and mail servers in front of this one.
receiving.enforceDmarcHint: Mail that breaks the sender's policy is refused instead of going to spam.
receiving.trustedRelaysHint: IP addresses or networks, one per line. UwUMail does their sender checks.

spamLog.enabledHint: Writes down what the filter did with each arriving message. Without it you never see why a message was refused.
spamLog.cleanSubjectsHint: Off by default. The subject of anything held back is always kept -- without it the entry explains nothing. For mail that arrived normally it explains nothing and is only a risk.

spam.title: Spam filter
spam.intro: Scores mail from other servers and puts what looks suspicious into the spam folder. Mail from your own network is not scored.
spam.enabledHint: When it is off, only DMARC decides what goes to spam.
spam.blocklistsHint: Asks Spamhaus, SpamCop and Barracuda about the sending server. A list that does not answer does not count against the sender.
spam.bayesHint: Learns from marks and clear cases what spam looks like and scores it. It only counts once it has learned enough.
spam.junkScoreHint: From this score on, mail goes to the spam folder.
spam.greylistScoreHint: Suspicious senders we do not know yet have to try again a little later. The same value as for spam turns this off.
spam.greylistDelayHint: How long a sender that was held back has to wait.
spam.greylistHoldHint: Everyone sees under Spam filter what was held back for them, and can deliver or discard it right away. Off means delayed mail is turned away and forgotten, the way it used to be.
spam.rejectScoreHint: Leave empty to never refuse. Refused mail is gone, while the spam folder lets you look.
spam.trapsHint: Addresses that only collect spam: what arrives there is taken, taught to the learning filter and delivered nowhere. One per line. Only use addresses nobody writes to any more.

apps.title: Mail apps
apps.intro: Login and privacy when sending from apps.
apps.revealIp: Show the IP address in sent mail
apps.revealIpHint: By default UwUMail does not reveal where someone sent a message from.

antivirus.enabledHint: Needs a ClamAV running beside the server. Start it first: docker compose --profile antivirus up -d. Its first start takes a few minutes, until the signatures are there; afterwards the scanner needs about 1 GB of memory.
antivirus.addressHint: Host and port of clamd; clamav:3310 in the setup that ships with UwUMail.
antivirus.timeoutHint: After that the message goes on unchecked.
antivirus.maxSizeHint: Bigger messages go through unchecked; clamd refuses them anyway.

webmail.title: Mailbox in the browser
webmail.intro: Reading and writing mail at mail.…/mail, without a mail program.
webmail.enabledHint: Everyone signed in to the portal can open their mailbox here. Each account has its own switch under People; mail programs are not affected either way.

health.notChecked: The first check runs shortly after the start.

findings.dnsOk_one: The domain is set up correctly.
findings.dnsOk_other: All {{count}} domains are set up correctly.
findings.dnsPending_one: One domain has not been checked yet.
findings.dnsPending_other: {{count}} domains have not been checked yet.
findings.dnsUnavailable: DNS cannot be checked because the server cannot resolve names.
findings.certWaiting: The Let's Encrypt certificate has not arrived yet.
findings.deliveryNotChecked: Not checked yet whether mail can leave.
findings.outboundBlocked: The server cannot reach other mail servers ({{count}} domains affected).
findings.port25Blocked: Outgoing port 25 seems to be blocked.
findings.probeDns: The sending check could not resolve names.
findings.queueStuck_one: One message has been stuck for {{since}}.
findings.queueStuck_other: {{count}} messages are stuck, the oldest for {{since}}.
findings.manyBounces: {{count}} of {{total}} messages in the last 24 hours were refused.
findings.adminsSecure: Every admin uses a two-factor login.
findings.adminsWithoutSecondFactor_one: {{login}} is an admin without two-factor login.
findings.youWithoutSecondFactor: Your admin account has no two-factor login yet.
findings.tlsFailures_one: {{domain}}: one encrypted connection failed in the last week.
findings.tlsFailures_other: {{domain}}: {{count}} encrypted connections failed in the last week.
findings.dmarcOwnFailures_one: {{domain}}: one message from this server failed DMARC.
findings.dmarcOwnFailures_other: {{domain}}: {{count}} messages from this server failed DMARC.
findings.gatewayDown: No connection to the UwUMail Gateway for {{since}}.
findings.gatewayRefused: The UwUMail Gateway does not accept this server.
findings.gatewayPort25Blocked: The gateway cannot reach other mail servers on port 25.
findings.gatewayOutboundBlocked: Other mail servers cannot be reached through the gateway ({{count}} domains affected).
findings.virusScannerAway: The virus scanner does not answer. Until it is back, mail is delivered unchecked and says so in its headers.
findings.virusSignaturesOld: The virus signatures are {{since}} old. The scanner is not fetching new ones any more.

hints.noDomains: Without a domain the server cannot receive mail.
hints.dnsDomain: The domain page shows which record is missing or wrong.
hints.certWaiting: The server must be reachable under its name on port 80. Until then mail apps warn when connecting.
hints.certSelfSigned: Mail apps warn when connecting. For real use, use Let's Encrypt or your own certificate files.
hints.certWrongName: Mail apps warn when connecting. Check the hostname in the configuration.
hints.certExpired: Mail apps can no longer connect securely. Renew the certificate.
hints.certExpiresSoon: It is usually renewed in time. The log shows why that fails.
hints.relayLogin: Check the username and password under Settings → Sending.
hints.relayTls: Check the port and encryption under Settings → Sending.
hints.relayUnreachable: Check the relay's address and port. Mail waits in the queue meanwhile.
hints.outboundBlocked: Many internet connections block port 25. A relay under Settings → Sending helps then.
hints.port25Blocked: Many internet connections block port 25. A relay under Settings → Sending helps then.
hints.queueStuck: The queue shows what is going wrong.
hints.manyBounces: Other servers refuse mail, e.g. because of SPF, DKIM or the IP address's reputation.
hints.diskLow: When storage is full, the server cannot accept mail any more.
hints.mailboxesNearlyFull: Full mailboxes stop accepting mail. Raise the limit or ask them to clean up.
hints.adminsWithoutSecondFactor: Whoever guesses an admin's password can manage the whole server.
hints.youWithoutSecondFactor: Under Security you set up an authenticator app or a passkey in two minutes.
hints.tlsFailures: Reports on the domain page show what went wrong, for example an expired certificate.
hints.dmarcOwnFailures: Usually the server is missing from the SPF record or DKIM does not match. The domain page shows the records.
hints.gatewayDown: Mail waits in the queue meanwhile. Check that the gateway is running and that your server may send UDP to it.
hints.gatewayRefused: Pair the gateway again under Server → Setup.
hints.gatewayPort25Blocked: Many VPS providers block outgoing port 25. Ask their support to open it; a relay helps until then.
hints.gatewayOutboundBlocked: Many VPS providers block outgoing port 25. Ask their support to open it; a relay helps until then.

secondFactor.title: One more step
secondFactor.totpIntro: Enter the six-digit code from your authenticator app.
secondFactor.passkeyIntro: Confirm the login with your passkey.
secondFactor.recoveryIntro: Enter one of your recovery codes. Each code works only once.
secondFactor.useApp: Use a code from the app

security.title: Security
security.intro: Password, two-factor login, app passwords and where you are logged in.
security.adminReminder: You are an admin, but your account has no two-factor login yet. Whoever guesses your password can manage the whole server.

confirm.title: Confirm your password
confirm.body: For safety, this change needs your password once more. After that you won't be asked again for ten minutes.

twoFactor.title: Two-factor login
twoFactor.on: On. Logging in to the portal also needs your app or a passkey.
twoFactor.off: Off. Your password alone is enough to log in.
twoFactor.explain: With a second factor, nobody gets into your account with just your password. Mail apps then log in with app passwords.

totp.title: Authenticator app
totp.inactive: For example Aegis, 2FAS, Proton Pass or Google Authenticator.
totp.step1: Open your authenticator app and add a new account.
totp.step2: Scan the QR code or type in the key.
totp.step3: Enter the code the app shows.
totp.qrLabel: QR code for the authenticator app
totp.manual: Can't scan? This key works too:

passkeys.title: Passkeys
passkeys.explain: Fingerprint, face recognition, Windows Hello or a security key. No code to type.
passkeys.addBody: Your browser will ask for the passkey in a moment. Give it a name first so you recognise it later.
passkeys.name: Name
passkeys.unavailable: Passkeys can only be added when you open the portal on {{hostname}}.

recovery.title: Recovery codes
recovery.shownOnce: Keep these codes safe, for example printed or in a password manager. They are only shown now and help you when your phone or passkey is gone.

appPasswords.title: App passwords
appPasswords.explain: For mail apps on your phone or computer. Each app gets its own password that you can revoke any time without changing your main password.
appPasswords.requiredBySecondFactor: With two-factor login, mail apps log in with app passwords only.
appPasswords.requireLabel: Mail apps only with app passwords
appPasswords.requireHint: Your main password then only works here in the portal.
appPasswords.name: What for?
appPasswords.scopeMailHint: For mail apps using IMAP or JMAP. JMAP apps can send with it too.
appPasswords.scopeSmtpHint: For apps, printers or scripts that only send.
appPasswords.scopeDavHint: For apps using CalDAV and CardDAV, like Calendar and Contacts on an iPhone.
appPasswords.createdBody: Enter this in the app “{{name}}”. The password is only shown now.
appPasswords.revokeBody: The app can no longer log in until you enter a new app password.

password.title: Change password
password.hint: At least 10 characters. A sentence of several words is easy to remember.
password.changed: Password changed. Other browsers were logged out.

events.passwordChosenWithLink: New password chosen through a link
events.appsNeedAppPassword: Mail apps now need app passwords
events.appsMayUseMainPassword: Mail apps may use the main password again
events.mainPasswordRefused: A mail app used the main password ({{protocol}}) and was refused

fetch.title: Fetched mailboxes
fetch.intro: Mailboxes at other providers that this server empties for you.

card.title: Your fetched mailboxes
card.hint: Fetched mail lands in your inbox and goes through the spam filter like any other.

empty.title: No mailbox here yet
empty.body: Add an address at another provider and this server will fetch its mail regularly.

actions.removeConfirm: Stop fetching {{address}}? Mail that already arrived stays where it is.

form.addressHint: The address whose mail should come here.
form.hostHint: Guessed from the address. Enter it here if the name is different.
form.usernameHint: Leave empty when it is the address itself.
form.passwordHint: iCloud and Google need an app password, not the one you sign in with.
form.newPasswordHint: Leave empty to keep the stored one.
form.needPassword: Without a password this server cannot get into the mailbox.
form.afterFetchHint: Only what really arrived here is ever deleted.
form.junkHint: What the provider sorted out is judged again here — its verdict only counts as a hint.
form.added: Mailbox added. The first run only writes down where things stand.
form.sendHint: Replies go out through the provider, otherwise its DMARC policy takes them apart at the recipient.
form.smtpHostHint: Guessed from the address. The password is the same one that fetches.

about.title: Worth knowing
about.spam: Fetched mail is judged again here. What the provider thought was spam counts as a hint and does not decide on its own.
about.first: The first run brings nothing, it only writes down where the folders stand. Mail that is already there comes over with the server's migration command.
about.password: The password only goes in and never comes out again. The server needs it to sign in at the provider and keeps it sealed.

mailbox.title: Forwarding and away
mailbox.intro: Where else your mail goes, and what senders hear while you are away.

forwarding.title: Forwarding
forwarding.explain: Mail to you also goes to these addresses. Addresses on other servers get a mail first and have to confirm the forwarding.
forwarding.onlyLocal: On this server you can only forward to people on the same server.
forwarding.pending: Waiting for the address to confirm
forwarding.keepCopy: Keep a copy in my mailbox
forwarding.keepCopyHint: Off: forwarded mail only goes to the addresses above.

vacation.title: Away message
vacation.enabledHint: Each sender gets at most one reply a week. Newsletters and machines get none.
vacation.subject: Subject
vacation.textPlaceholder: Hello, I'm away until … and will reply afterwards.

forwardConfirm.title: Confirm forwarding
forwardConfirm.body: {{from}} would like to forward mail to {{address}}.
forwardConfirm.confirmedBody: Mail to {{from}} now also arrives at {{address}}.
forwardConfirm.declinedBody: You won't get mail from {{from}}. The forwarding was deleted.
forwardConfirm.invalidBody: It was used already or is older than seven days.

addresses.intro: The addresses you get mail at and how much space it takes.
addresses.title: Your addresses
addresses.closed: Creating your own addresses is not open on this server right now. Ask the admin.
addresses.explain: Extra addresses arrive in the same mailbox. Handy for signing up at shops or clubs. A deleted address stays reserved for you for 30 days.
addresses.deleted: {{address}} deleted, reserved for you for 30 days
addresses.releasedHint: Mail to these addresses is refused until you take them back or the time runs out.

storage.title: Storage
storage.emptyBody: The messages in it are deleted for good. Messages that are in another folder too stay there.

welcome.title: Welcome to UwUMail
welcome.body: A few steps and your mail server is ready: first your admin account and the domain, then the DNS records, sending, and a test message at the end.
welcome.codeHint: The server writes it to its log on start while there is no admin yet.
welcome.whereSimple: To find it, run this command on the server in the UwUMail folder. The line with “/setup” has the code.
welcome.wherePro: Log line: “no admin yet: open https://…/setup and enter the one-time code …”

closed.title: This server is already set up
closed.body: Log in with your admin account. The checks are under Server → Setup afterwards.

noCode.title: No one-time code right now
noCode.body: Restart the server. While there is no admin, it writes a new code to its log.

admin.title: Your admin account
admin.body: You get a mail address on your domain. You use it to log in here and manage the server.
admin.domainHint: The domain for your mail addresses, for example example.com.
admin.name: Name
admin.nameHint: This is the sender name others see.
admin.hostnameNote: The server is called {{hostname}}. That is set in the .env file.

dns.title: DNS records for {{domain}}
dns.body: For other servers to accept your mail and send mail to you, the domain needs a few records at your DNS provider. Add the missing ones and check again.
dns.hostnameNote: {{hostname}} also needs an A or AAAA record pointing to your server.
dns.later: New DNS records sometimes take a while to show up everywhere. You can go on anyway and look again later under Domains.
dns.gatewayHost: With a gateway: {{hostname}} (A/AAAA) has to point to {{addresses}}, and the reverse DNS of those addresses to {{hostname}}, set at the VPS provider.

cloudflare.title: Add at Cloudflare
cloudflare.body: If the domain is at Cloudflare, I add the missing records for you. The token is only used for this one request and never stored.
cloudflare.tokenHint: At Cloudflare, create a token under “Profile → API Tokens” with the permission “Zone → DNS → Edit” for this domain.
cloudflare.replaceHint: Unticked records stay as they are.
cloudflare.tidy: Bring the spelling in line with UwUMail
cloudflare.tidyHint: These records work. With a tick I write them the way UwUMail would publish them.
cloudflare.tidyWarning: Careful with MX and SPF: I write exactly my own value. Other senders or a mail server in front of this one that are listed there fall away.
cloudflare.quotesOnly: Nothing is missing. I can still check whether the records sit in quotes at Cloudflare and add them where they do not.

sending.title: Sending and receiving
sending.body: I check whether mail gets out of the server and whether other mail servers can reach it.
sending.running: Checking, this can take up to a minute …
sending.honest: For this the server calls itself on its public address. Whether port 25 is really open to the internet only shows once a reply from outside arrives in the test message step.
sending.relayBody: A relay is a mail server that passes your mail on, for example from your hosting provider or a sending service. You get the credentials there.

checks.title: Reverse DNS and blocklists
checks.body: Many mail servers check whether your server's address has a matching name (PTR) and whether it is on a spam list.
checks.blocklistsBody: This asks Spamhaus, SpamCop and Barracuda about the address other servers see as the sender. It only happens when you ask for it.

testMail.title: Test message
testMail.body: I send a message to your new mailbox. With a second address at another provider you also test the way out and back.
testMail.arrived: It arrived! Your mailbox accepts mail.
testMail.slow: After a minute the message is still not there. See whether it is stuck in the queue:
testMail.externalBody: I also send the message to another address of yours. Reply to it from there: when the reply arrives here, mail from outside reaches you.
testMail.externalWaiting: Sent to {{address}}. Reply to it from there, I'm waiting …
testMail.replied: The reply from {{address}} arrived. Mail from outside reaches you.

done.title: Done!
done.summary: You can find the checks again at any time under Server → Setup.
done.next: Next: add people and turn on two-factor login for your account.

page.title: Setup
page.intro: The checks from the setup assistant: sending, receiving, reverse DNS, blocklists and a test message.
page.domainsBody: Records are checked per domain. If a domain is at Cloudflare, I can add them there.

lines.directOk: The server reaches other mail servers directly on port 25 ({{target}}).
lines.port25Blocked: No connection to other mail servers on port 25 ({{target}}).
lines.upstream: Another mail server receives the mail first and passes it on to this one.
lines.inboundOk: Port 25 on {{ip}} answers, and it is this server.
lines.ptrUnconfirmed: {{ip}} is called {{name}}, but that name does not point back to the address.
lines.ptrPrivate: The server name only points to private addresses. The public address and its name cannot be seen from here.
lines.ptrRelay: Mail leaves through {{host}}. Its reverse DNS is up to the relay provider.
lines.noPublicAddress: There is no public address to check.
lines.publicAddressUnknown: The public address could not be found.
lines.homeConnection: According to Spamhaus, {{ip}} is a home or dynamic connection.
lines.ptrGeneric: The reverse DNS of {{ip}} is not a name of its own ({{name}}).
lines.providerHetzner: Hetzner Cloud blocks outgoing ports 25 and 465.
lines.gatewayOk: The gateway reaches other mail servers on port 25 ({{target}}).
lines.gatewayPort25Blocked: The gateway cannot reach other mail servers on port 25 ({{target}}).
lines.inboundSelfCall: Port 25 on {{ip}} does not answer from here.
lines.gatewayConnected: Connected to the UwUMail Gateway. Other servers see {{addresses}}.
lines.gatewayDns: {{hostname}} has to point to {{addresses}}, and the reverse DNS of those addresses to {{hostname}}.
lines.gatewayRefusedNotPaired: The gateway does not know this server.
lines.gatewayRefusedWrongToken: The pairing code is not valid, or not any more.
lines.gatewayRefusedOtherServer: The gateway already belongs to another server.
lines.gatewayRefusedVersion: Gateway and server speak different tunnel versions.
lines.gatewayUpToDate: The gateway is up to date ({{name}}).
lines.gatewaySecurityUpdates: {{count}} updates wait on the gateway, {{security}} of them security updates.
lines.gatewayUpdates: {{count}} updates wait on the gateway, none of them security updates.
lines.gatewayAutomaticSecurity: The gateway installs security updates by itself.
lines.gatewayReboot: The gateway is waiting for a restart.
lines.gatewayNewRelease: A newer version of the gateway's system waits: {{release}}.
lines.gatewayProtected: The gateway runs {{firewall}} and fail2ban. {{banned}} addresses are kept out, {{fromServer}} of them at this server's request.
lines.gatewayNoFirewall: The gateway has no firewall running.
lines.gatewayNoFail2ban: The gateway runs {{firewall}}, but no fail2ban.
lines.gatewayTrusted: The gateway never locks this server out ({{addresses}}).

hints.directDns: Check that the server has a working DNS resolver.
hints.port25Blocked: Many internet connections and some cloud providers block outgoing port 25. Ask your provider to open it, or send mail through a relay.
hints.relayLogin: Check the user name and password.
hints.relayUnreachable: Check the relay's address and port. Until then, mail waits in the queue.
hints.noAddress: Add an A record (IPv4) and, if possible, an AAAA record (IPv6) for the server name at your DNS provider.
hints.privateOnly: The internet cannot reach the server like this. Behind a router, port 25 has to be forwarded to the server, and the public DNS record has to point to the public address.
hints.inboundOther: The router or firewall probably forwards port 25 to another device.
hints.inboundClosed: Check the firewall and port forwarding. Some routers cannot reach themselves on the public address; then only the test message from outside tells for sure.
hints.ptrMissing: Without a matching name, many mail servers reject mail. The PTR record is set by whoever provides the IP address, often in their customer panel. It should be {{hostname}}.
hints.ptrUnconfirmed: Have the PTR record changed to {{hostname}}, or add an A or AAAA record for {{name}} with {{ip}}.
hints.ptrOtherName: {{hostname}} is better. The PTR record is changed by whoever provides the IP address.
hints.ptrPrivate: If the server is reachable from outside on another address, check that address's PTR record with the provider.
hints.listed: The list's website explains why the address is listed and how to get it removed.
hints.listUnknown: Some lists do not answer through public DNS resolvers such as 8.8.8.8 or 1.1.1.1.
hints.homeConnection: Big mail providers do not accept mail straight from such addresses, and you usually cannot set reverse DNS there. A UwUMail Gateway on a small VPS solves both.
hints.spamhausListed: For a fixed address: find the cause (such as an infected device) and ask Spamhaus to remove it. Otherwise a gateway helps.
hints.spamhausUnknown: Spamhaus does not answer questions through big public DNS resolvers. With a resolver of your own the check works.
hints.ptrGeneric: Set the reverse DNS to your server's name at the provider of the address. On home connections that is usually not possible.
hints.providerHetzner: Unblocking is only possible after a month and the first paid invoice, on request and case by case. That makes Hetzner Cloud a poor choice for mail servers and gateways.
hints.providerStrato: STRATO support opens port 25 when you ask.
hints.providerIonos: IONOS customer service opens port 25 by phone once reverse DNS and SPF are in place.
hints.gatewayPort25Blocked: Ask the VPS provider to open port 25. Until then you can send through a relay; that also goes through the gateway.
hints.inboundSelfCall: Many routers cannot call themselves. The test mail shows whether mail from outside arrives.
hints.gatewayConnecting: Is the gateway running (systemctl status uwumail-gateway), and may your server send UDP to the gateway?
hints.gatewayDns: You set both at your DNS provider and at the VPS provider.
hints.gatewayRefusedNotPaired: Get a pairing code on the VPS with uwumail-gateway code.
hints.gatewayRefusedWrongToken: Get a new pairing code on the VPS with uwumail-gateway code.
hints.gatewayRefusedOtherServer: Undo the old pairing on the VPS with uwumail-gateway unpair, then pair again.
hints.gatewayRefusedVersion: Update the gateway and the server to the same version.
hints.gatewaySecurityUpdates: Over SSH onto the gateway, and install them: {{ssh}}
hints.gatewayUpdates: Over SSH onto the gateway, and install them: {{ssh}}
hints.gatewayReboot: While it restarts, other mail servers are asked to try again later, and they do. Nothing is lost.
hints.gatewayNewRelease: A version jump wants company: do-release-upgrade on the gateway, when you have time and a second SSH session open.
hints.gatewayNoFirewall: Run the install command again; it sets up ufw as well.
hints.gatewayNoFail2ban: Run the install command again; it sets up fail2ban as well.
hints.gatewayTrusted: This address is on the gateway's exception list, so no ban can lock out your own server. When your address changes, the gateway swaps it on the next connection.

reach.title: How can your server be reached?
reach.body: Nyu looks at how other mail servers see your server: public address, Spamhaus, network and port 25. Then you decide whether mail goes directly or through a UwUMail Gateway.
reach.directNote: Your server receives and sends mail itself. That needs a fixed public address, port 25 in both directions and reverse DNS with its name.

recommend.gateway: Nyu recommends a UwUMail Gateway: many mail servers would not accept mail from this connection.
recommend.direct: Looks good: your server can send and receive mail itself.
recommend.unknown: Your public address could not be found. Check the connection and try again.
recommend.paired: Your server sends and receives through the UwUMail Gateway.

gateway.title: UwUMail Gateway
gateway.howTo: Rent a small VPS with a fixed address and an open port 25, install the gateway there and copy the pairing code from its log or from uwumail-gateway code.
gateway.vpsAlone: The VPS belongs to the gateway alone: no second mail or web server, no Plesk, no other services. The gateway needs ports 25, 80, 443, 465, 587 and 993 for itself, and whatever else runs there hangs on your reachability too.
gateway.codeHint: Starts with uwugw1 and works once.
gateway.forgetBody: Your server then sends and receives mail itself again. Change the DNS records back too, or mail stops arriving.
gateway.fromConfig: This pairing is set as gateway.code in the configuration. If you forget the gateway here, remove the code as well. Otherwise the server tries to pair again on the next start with a new key, the gateway refuses it, and mail to other servers waits in the queue. To pair again later, run uwumail-gateway unpair on the gateway and use the new code.
gateway.paired: Paired, the tunnel is coming up.

machine.title: The VPS
machine.hint: The gateway last looked on {{time}}. While one of these runs the gateway is away for a moment — mail that arrives meanwhile is delivered again later by the sending server.

restore.offer: Is this server standing in for one that is gone?
restore.title: Put a backup back
restore.body: Say where the backups are. This server fetches a snapshot from there and becomes the server it came from — with all its mail, accounts and settings.
restore.privateKeyHint: The key the old server reached the backup server with. This machine has none that is listed there yet — and the old one cannot list it any more.
restore.recoveryHint: Only needed when the backups are encrypted.
restore.recoveryNeeded: The backups there are encrypted. Without the recovery key this cannot go on.
restore.none: There are no snapshots on this backup server.
restore.warning: Everything on this server is replaced by it. On a freshly set up server that is nothing — which is exactly what this is for.

running.title: Fetching the backup
running.body: Nyu is unpacking the snapshot. Depending on its size and the line this takes a few minutes.
running.wait: The server fetches the backup and restarts afterwards. You can leave this page open.
running.then: After that, log in with the account that is in the backup — not with a new one.

updates.title: Updates
updates.intro: Which version is running, what is new, and what installs it.
updates.notChecked: Have not looked for updates yet.
updates.edgeBehind_one: There is {{count}} new commit on main:
updates.edgeBehind_other: There are {{count}} new commits on main:
updates.checkHint: Asks GitHub once a day whether there is a new version.
updates.onTheMachine: Updating happens on the machine, not from here — the script also brings a new compose.yaml along, which a container replacing itself never could.

backups.title: Backups
backups.intro: Every night the server backs up mail, settings, calendars and contacts to an SFTP server, like a NAS. After the first time it only uploads what is new.

status.title: Status
status.sizes: {{total}} backed up, {{uploaded}} of it uploaded now

target.title: Backup server
target.explain: Where backups go. The folder is created if it does not exist; use one per server.
target.pathHint: Relative to the home directory, or starting with /
target.keyAfterSave: After saving, the server makes its own key and shows it here.
target.publicKeyHint: Add this line to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of the user on the backup server:
target.passwordKept: Leave empty to keep the stored password.
target.testFirst: The connection works. The server presented {{hostKey}}; from now on it has to be this key.

schedule.encryptedHint: Recommended: then nobody can read the mail on the backup server. To restore you need the recovery key.
schedule.encryptedFixed: There are backups already, so this stays as it is.

snapshots.title: Snapshots
snapshots.restoreHint: Restoring works on the command line, into an empty data directory, also on a new machine. The command asks for the recovery key.
snapshots.restoreHere: A snapshot can be put back here, or on the command line into an empty data directory — including on a brand new machine where no server runs yet:

recovery.title: Recovery key
recovery.explain: Without this key the backups cannot be read anymore, not even by me. Write it down or keep it in your password manager, apart from this server.

restore.title: Put a backup back
restore.warning: Everything on this server is replaced by what is in the backup: mail, accounts, settings, calendars, contacts. Anything that arrived since is gone afterwards.
restore.how: The server fetches the backup, then stops itself, and the next start puts the files in place — while it runs it is working on exactly the database that would be replaced. Docker brings the container back by itself; it takes a few minutes.
restore.keepGatewayHint: The backup carries the pairing of the server it came from. If this machine is its replacement, the one here is the right one.
restore.fetching: Fetching the backup {{snapshot}} ({{size}}). The server restarts afterwards.
restore.fetchFailed: The backup could not be fetched: {{error}}. Nothing was touched.
restore.staged: A backup from {{hostname}}, the state of {{time}}, is here. It goes in at the next start — restart the server.
restore.lastDone: Put back: the state of {{time}} from {{hostname}}.
restore.lastFailed: Putting the backup back did not work: {{error}}. The server is running on what was here before.
restore.backupsOff: Backups are switched off now. The backup carried the old server's target — turn them on again once the target is right.
restore.keptGateway: This machine's gateway pairing was kept, not the one from the backup.
restore.oldDatabase: The database from before is in the data directory as uwumail.db.replaced.*. Delete it once you are sure.

account.title: Spam filter
account.intro: Senders you always let through or sort out, and what the spam filter learned from you.

greylist.title: Waiting messages
greylist.explain: When a message looks suspicious, the server asks the sending server to try again later. Real mail servers do that within a few minutes; spammers mostly never do. Until then the message waits here. What you decide here is about this one message — letting a sender through for good is under Filter, in your sender list.
greylist.off: The server is not keeping delayed messages at the moment, so this list stays empty.
greylist.emptyHint: Delayed messages wait here until they arrive by themselves or you decide about them.

done.delivered: It is in your inbox now.
done.discarded: Gone — even if the sender tries again.

confirm.title: Discard this message?
confirm.body: The message is deleted. If the sender tries again later, it will not come back.
confirm.bodySpam: The message is deleted and the spam filter learns from it. If the sender tries again later, it will not come back.

limits.title: Your limits
limits.explain: Every message from outside gets points, the more suspicious the more. Here you choose from how many points your mail goes to the spam folder or is not accepted at all. Empty means: like the server.
limits.junkHint: Server: from {{server}} points. Higher lets more through, lower sorts out more strictly.
limits.rejectHint: Server: from {{server}} points. You can be stricter, not more lenient. You never see refused mail.
limits.rejectHintNever: The server refuses nothing. You never see refused mail, not even in the spam folder.

admin.title: Spam filter
admin.intro: How the server scores mail from other servers, which senders it always lets through or turns away, and what the spam filter learned.

log.title: History
log.explain: What the filter did with each arriving message. The refused and the held-back ones are nowhere else at all -- they reach no mailbox, and the running log is empty after a restart.
log.off: The history is switched off. New decisions are not written down.
log.privacy: This says who writes to whom. Entries go after {{days}} days.
log.subjectsOn: Subjects are kept for mail that arrived normally too.
log.subjectsOff: Subjects are only kept for mail that was held back.
log.settingsIntro: What is written down, and for how long.
log.subject: Subject
log.authResults: What SPF, DKIM and DMARC found:

empty.title: Nothing here
empty.body: There are no entries for this filter.

log.clearBody: Every entry goes. The mail itself and what the filter learned are untouched.

bayes.title: Learning filter
bayes.explain: The filter remembers which words, links and senders show up in spam and in wanted mail. It compares new mail with that and gives points for or against it. When you mark a mail as spam or not spam, it learns from that. Only checksums are stored, not the words themselves.
bayes.explainAdmin: The server learns from clear cases and from everyone's marks. On top of that, each person has their own knowledge that comes only from their own marks. Only checksums are stored, not the words themselves.
bayes.off: The learning filter is turned off on this server. It keeps learning from marks but gives no points.
bayes.ownCounts: Your own knowledge counts and weighs more the more you mark.
bayes.ownLearning: Your own knowledge counts once {{minimum}} mails of each kind are learned. Until then, the server's knowledge decides.
bayes.serverLearning: The filter scores mail once {{minimum}} mails of each kind are learned.
bayes.queued_one: {{count}} mail is still waiting to be learned.
bayes.queued_other: {{count}} mails are still waiting to be learned.
bayes.learnHint: Learn once from existing mail: mail in the spam folder counts as spam, read mail in the inbox and archive older than two weeks as wanted.
bayes.learnHintAdmin: Learn once from everyone's mail: mail in the spam folder counts as spam, read mail in the inbox and archive older than two weeks as wanted.
bayes.learnQueued: {{spam}} spam mails and {{ham}} wanted mails are up for learning.
bayes.learnNothing: No suitable mail to learn from found.

senders.title: Allowed and blocked senders
senders.titleAdmin: Senders for the server and domains
senders.explain: Mail from allowed senders always goes to the inbox, mail from blocked ones to the spam folder. An address or domain only counts as allowed when SPF or DKIM confirm it, because anyone could fake a sender otherwise. What an admin blocks for the whole server or your domain still does not arrive.
senders.explainAdmin: Blocked senders are turned away while they hand in their mail. Allowed ones go to the inbox and never wait for greylisting; an address or domain only counts when SPF or DKIM confirm it. A block for the server or the domain always comes first, then a person's own list decides, then the domain's, and the server's last.
senders.valueHint: Email address, domain, IP address or network, host name like *.mail.example.com, or a pattern like *.tld or *newsletter* (* stands for any text)

words.title: Word list
words.titleAdmin: Word lists for the server and domains
words.explain: Words, phrases or expressions that make mail to you suspicious. Each match in the subject or text gives {{points}} points, all word lists together at most {{max}}. Paste Rspamd maps like /\sviagra\s/i as they are.
words.explainAdmin: Words, phrases or expressions that make mail suspicious, for the whole server or one domain. Each match in the subject or text gives {{points}} points, all word lists together at most {{max}}. Rspamd maps like /\sviagra\s/i can be pasted as they are or subscribed to by link.
words.entriesHint: One entry per line. A word matches whole words only, in any case; /expression/i is read as a regular expression. Lines starting with # are skipped.
words.subscribeTitle: Subscribe to a list by link
words.urlHint: https only. The server fetches the list right away and then daily; at most 1 MB.
words.subjectOnlyHint: For lists of subjects, e.g. from mailcow.
words.empty: No entries of your own yet.

feeds.title: Built-in lists
feeds.intro: Lists the server fetches regularly by itself. Each can be switched off; fetching them means the server contacts their providers.

urlhaus.label: Malware links (abuse.ch URLhaus)
urlhaus.hint: Links to malware that is online right now. A match gives 10 points. Needs the Auth-Key.

malware_bazaar.label: Malware attachments (abuse.ch MalwareBazaar)
malware_bazaar.hint: Files reported as malware in the last two days. A match gives 10 points. Needs the Auth-Key.

bad_subjects.label: Spam subjects (mailcow)
bad_subjects.hint: Subjects of current spam waves; each match counts like a word on the server's list. Only reachable without encryption, so expressions that match ordinary subjects are dropped.

disposable.label: Throwaway addresses (Rspamd)
disposable.hint: Senders with a throwaway address get 1.5 points.

freemail.label: Freemail providers (Rspamd)
freemail.hint: 2 points when replies are meant to go to a freemail address although the sender has none.

redirectors.label: Link shorteners (Rspamd)
redirectors.hint: 0.5 points for links through shorteners like bit.ly. The server never opens the links.

feeds.keyHint: Free at auth.abuse.ch, for non-commercial use only. Without a key the two abuse.ch lists stay off.
feeds.keySet: A key is stored. A new one replaces it.

antivirus.title: Virus scanner
antivirus.explain: With a ClamAV running beside the server, every message is shown to it before it is taken. If it finds something, the message is never accepted. If it does not answer, the message goes on and its headers say that nobody looked.
antivirus.settingsIntro: The scanner runs in its own container next to the server. How to start it: docs/antivirus.md.
antivirus.off: Off. Every message is taken without being shown to a scanner.
antivirus.found_one: In the last {{days}} days 1 message was turned away for a find.
antivirus.found_other: In the last {{days}} days {{count}} messages were turned away for a find.
antivirus.testHint: Sends the scanner the harmless EICAR test file that every scanner knows. If it reports it, the two really do talk to each other.
antivirus.testFound: The scanner recognised the test file: {{name}}
antivirus.testFailed: The scanner did not recognise the test file.

fetched.title: Fetched mail compared
fetched.explain: Of {{count}} messages fetched in the last {{days}} days: how often this server agreed with the provider, and where it did not.
fetched.empty: Nothing was fetched in the last {{days}} days, or the spam history is off.
fetched.agreedJunkHint: The provider had it in its junk folder, and it landed in Junk here too.
fetched.weCaughtHint: The provider let it through and this filter did not. That is the gain.
fetched.weLetThroughHint: The provider thought it was spam; here it reached the inbox. Either a false alarm of theirs, or something this filter does not know yet.
fetched.caveat: Counted from the spam history, so only as far back as that goes. The provider is a second opinion, not a yardstick.
